name: Single-Arm Plate Loaded Lat Pulldown
nameDa: Enarms pulldown i maskine med vægtskiver
grip: Semi-neutral or underhand grip on machine lever handle.
description: Pull an independent plate-loaded overhead lever arm downward with one arm, securing thighs under machine pads to target latissimus fibers.
setup: Load weight plates onto the working side lever horn.
Adjust the thigh pads so your legs are securely anchored with feet flat on the floor.
Sit upright, reach overhead with working arm to grasp the handle, and allow non-working arm to rest relaxed on your thigh.
Take up the load with arm extended overhead into a full lat stretch.
instructions: Drive the working elbow downward and slightly inward toward your hip along the lever's natural converging arc.
Keep your chest lifted with a natural thoracic arch, avoiding lateral torso leaning.
Squeeze the lat firmly as the handle reaches upper chest level.
Return the handle slowly upward until the arm is fully extended overhead under control.
Complete the set, then switch to the other arm.
cues: Drive elbow straight down to the hip.
commonMistakes: Leaning or twisting the torso sideways to heave the lever down.
Letting the non-working arm assist the movement.
Letting the lever slam against the top stops.

logging.example: One 20 kg plate loaded on working lever: record 20 kg per side.
logging.note: Plate-loaded machines feature independent lever arms with specific pivot mechanics; record the plate mass loaded on that working side.

variantNote: Unilateral vertical pull on a plate-loaded machine with independent converging lever arms, isolating each lat.
